title: The bot's host moves to its own VM; J01, J05 and J06 pass there
gate: BARKBOT_HOST_NAME="BarkBot VM" BARKBOT_LIVE_DIR=vm npm run turn:live -- --bot <the VM's Main Bot> (J01; add --resume for J06, restarting barkbot-host on the VM at the prompt) and node scripts/cancel-live.mjs --session <its conversation> --ssh barkbot@<vm> (J05). Owner-run: the owner's Barkpark login and the VM online. Records: parity/live/vm/turn.json, cancel.json, resume.json.
evidence: The VM: Hetzner warm-52d0bbcf (x86_64, Ubuntu 22.04), taken out of Barkpark Cloud's warm pool (its pool row deleted with the owner's approval, 2026-11-19; labelled barkbot-host). User barkbot, one locked folder ~/BarkBot/home, barkpark-chat-host built from Barkpark origin/main 66059cd3bc under systemd (barkbot-host.service, restarts on failure), Claude Code 2.1.328 signed in by the owner, bp on PATH (Barkpark refuses a registered host's turn without task_hands: 422 chat_unsupported). Enrolled as 'BarkBot VM' beside 'BarkBot Mac'; a conversation is pinned to one computer when it is made, and the app picks the computer by name (BARKBOT_HOST_NAME). Seen live 2026-11-19, every turn checked to land on the VM's conversation and its Claude session: J01 a reply in 8.2 s, 6 + 6 bubbles, the same after a reload. J06 the VM's host restarted within 2 s (systemctl restart) and the bot gave the code back. J05 at the plumbing only (C1: the app has no Stop): an interrupt 409 characters into a long reply ended the turn as turn_completed interrupted in 640 ms, and the host program's claude child went from 1 to 0. Not yet: the first message to a new conversation is never sent (the app's stream proxy waits for Barkpark's first body byte, 30 s on an empty conversation; task-7ec7bb04a1125c4d), so J01 ran on a conversation that already had turns. The Mac's host still runs; the cut-over (the app's default computer, then stopping the Mac) is not done.
